Gaussian completion with an explicit category observation model

Source: R/model.R
catmech_model.Rd

Replaces all flagged measurements and missing values using a conditional Gaussian model. Trusted numeric measurements are kept exactly. The default ignores categories; optional exact or externally specified noisy categories enter through a likelihood, not by forcing trusted values to change.

Usage

catmech_model(
  data,
  value,
  predictors,
  flag = NULL,
  flag_yes = "Yes",
  flag_no = "No",
  category = NULL,
  thresholds = NULL,
  levels = NULL,
  category_mode = c("ignore", "exact", "noisy"),
  confusion = NULL,
  m = 20L,
  seed = 1L,
  burnin = 200L,
  iterations = 400L,
  chains = 4L
)

Arguments

data

A data frame. Original columns, values and category labels are preserved separately and in every completion except for the target cells.

value

Name of the numeric target column.

predictors

Explicit names of complete covariates, including the downstream outcome when appropriate. Use `character(0)` for an intercept.

flag

Optional quality-flag column. All `flag_yes` measurements are treated as unavailable, including false-positive flags.

flag_yes, flag_no

Labels for suspect and non-suspect measurements. Missing flags are treated as non-suspect, an explicit trust assumption.

category

Optional category column. Ignored without validation when `category_mode = "ignore"`. Missing categories contribute no likelihood.

thresholds

Numeric category endpoints. For informative categories, the first must be `-Inf` and the last `Inf`.

levels

Ordered category labels with length one less than thresholds.

category_mode

`"ignore"` (default), `"exact"`, or `"noisy"`.

confusion

For noisy categories, a numeric matrix with named rows for true categories and named columns for observed categories, both matching `levels`. Entries are nonnegative and each row sums to one. These fixed probabilities must come from external validation or declared sensitivity assumptions; this function does not estimate them or their uncertainty.

m

Number of completions, at least two.

seed

Nonnegative integer seed. The caller's RNG state is restored.

burnin

Discarded Gibbs iterations per chain.

iterations

Retained diagnostic iterations per chain, at least 100 when informative categories require Gibbs sampling.

chains

Number of independent Gibbs chains, at least four when used.

Value

A `catmech_result` with `original`, `completed`, `mids`, `audit`, `diagnostics`, `spec`, `manifest`, and `model_diagnostics`. The `mids` object contains the target and selected predictors, plus a constant auxiliary column for an intercept-only model. Its completions are externally generated; it must not be continued using `mice.mids`.

Details

The model is `Y | X, beta, sigma ~ Normal(X beta, sigma^2)`, with the reference prior `p(beta, sigma^2) proportional to 1 / sigma^2`. The trusted design must have full column rank, positive residual degrees of freedom and positive residual variance. Globally aliased predictors must be removed explicitly. Flag removal and missingness must be ignorable given the selected predictors. This is not a model of the observed corrupted measurement or an estimate of its probability of being wrong.

Ignored categories use independent posterior predictive draws from trusted data. Informative categories use Gibbs data augmentation: sample latent bins with probabilities proportional to category likelihood times normal interval mass; draw values from those truncated normals; and update regression parameters using completed data. Equal rows in a confusion matrix contain no information about the target and reduce to the independent-draw engine.

Gibbs diagnostics use `posterior` rank-normalized split/folded R-hat and bulk and tail effective sample size. An R-hat above 1.05, bulk or tail ESS below `100 * chains`, or a nonfinite diagnostic produces a `catmech_convergence_error`. Its `model_diagnostics` field retains all traces and the diagnostic summary. These checks do not prove convergence or calibration. Completions are spaced across retained iterations and balanced across chains; they are not claimed independent.

Exact-category conflicts with trusted values are errors. With noisy categories, a trusted conflict is allowed only when its supplied likelihood is positive. Recorded categories are never overwritten to make a completion agree with them. Rubin pooling remains conditional on model adequacy and compatibility with the intended analysis, especially outside a linear-Gaussian analysis setting.

Examples

d <- simulate_catmech_lab(100, seed = 8)
fit <- catmech_model(d, "lab_value", c("age", "inflammation", "outcome"),
  flag = "outlier_flag", m = 3, seed = 12)
fit$manifest$engine
#> [1] "gaussian_model"
